aboutH2: The Healing Institute: Residential Addiction and Mental Health Care on Gabriola Island
intro: The Healing Institute is a private residential centre for addiction, mental health concerns and concurrent disorders at Taylor Bay on Gabriola Island, a short ferry ride from Nanaimo. It moved here from Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay in early 2026 and now shares a 6.77-acre oceanfront campus with The Haven, a learning centre that has been on the site since 1983.

Care starts with an assessment and an individual plan. From there it combines counselling, CBT and DBT, medical and nursing support (including withdrawal management when needed), and daily wellness time with yoga, art therapy, nature and chef-cooked meals. Lifetime continuing care is included for every participant.

pillars.title: An Oceanfront Campus at Taylor Bay
pillars.body: The campus sits on Gabriola Island's northwest shore, a few minutes from the Descanso Bay ferry terminal. It covers 6.77 acres with 426 feet of shoreline, and the land runs from coastal forest and walking trails down to flat sandstone ledges at the water. Residents live and meet in several timber buildings with decks and a glass sunroom facing the Strait of Georgia. The Haven, a not-for-profit learning centre that has been here since 1983, shares the site and keeps running its own retreats and workshops.

pillars.title: Continuing Care for Life, and a Weekly Family Group
pillars.body: Planning for home starts during treatment, and Continuing Care Coordinator Sepideh Sadeghi works with each person on what the first weeks back will look like. Once residential care ends, every participant keeps lifetime access to continuing care. The centre's recovery.com profile describes online follow-up sessions, aftercare groups and recovery coaching. Families have their own free group, the Family Freedom Program, which meets on Zoom every Monday at 5:30 p.m. Pacific and works through topics like attachment, anger and codependency.

pillars.title: A Clinical Team With Long Addiction Experience
pillars.body: Chief Clinical Officer Elizabeth Loudon is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with more than 23 years in addiction treatment, including clinical director roles at Edgewood West and Cedars at Cobble Hill. Clinical Director Lliam Broderick oversees the day-to-day therapy program, and nurse practitioner Jackie Muth leads medical care. Executive Director Brett Johnson has 14 years in recovery himself and previously ran men's sober housing. Counsellors on the team bring training in DBT, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Seeking Safety, Internal Family Systems and Gottman couples work.

overview: The Healing Institute treats substance use and mental health together, on the view that problems like trauma, depression and anxiety often sit underneath addiction. It is run by ROSC Solutions Group, which operates treatment, recovery and related services across Western Canada. Men and women attend together, according to the centre's recovery.com profile.

location.heading: The Healing Institute in Gabriola, British Columbia
location.intro: The Healing Institute is at Taylor Bay on Gabriola Island, one of the Gulf Islands, a 20-minute BC Ferries crossing from downtown Nanaimo to Descanso Bay and then a short drive. From Vancouver the trip takes about 3 to 4 hours with the Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay ferry and the Gabriola crossing, Victoria is about 2 hours away by car and ferry, and Courtenay and the Comox Valley are roughly an hour and 45 minutes.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and its public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Where is The Healing Institute now?
faqs.a: The Healing Institute is at 240 Davis Road on Gabriola Island, BC, at Taylor Bay on the island's northwest shore. It moved there from Forbidden Plateau near Courtenay and announced the move as complete on March 12, 2026. The campus is shared with The Haven, which still runs its own programs on the site.

faqs.q: How do I get to Gabriola Island?
faqs.a: Gabriola is reached by a BC Ferries crossing of about 20 minutes from downtown Nanaimo to Descanso Bay. From Vancouver, take the Horseshoe Bay to Departure Bay ferry to Nanaimo first, so the whole trip usually takes 3 to 4 hours with sailing waits. Ask admissions about arrival times before you book.

faqs.q: What level of care does The Healing Institute offer?
faqs.a: It is a residential program, so you live on site for the length of treatment. Medical and nursing staff provide medically supported withdrawal management when it is needed, and lifetime continuing care follows discharge. The centre does not list a standalone outpatient program.

The centre's website does not publish a fixed length. Its recovery.com profile gives a typical stay of 6 to 8 weeks, with residential stays ranging from 14 to 90 days. Admissions will confirm the length once your assessment is done.

faqs.q: Does The Healing Institute offer detox?
faqs.a: Yes, in a supported form. The program page says medical and nursing care includes medically supported withdrawal management when required, along with assessment, medication management and health monitoring. Tell admissions what you are using so they can plan this before you arrive.

faqs.q: How much does The Healing Institute cost?
faqs.a: The centre does not publish its fees on its website or on recovery.com. It is a private, fee-based program, and admissions goes over costs during a free 15-minute consultation. A Medicard partner logo on the site suggests financing may be available, so ask about it when you call.

faqs.q: Is The Healing Institute publicly funded?
faqs.a: No, it is a private centre and does not describe any coverage through Island Health or another BC health authority. Some extended health or employer plans may reimburse part of private treatment, so check your plan and ask admissions for the paperwork you would need.

faqs.q: What conditions does The Healing Institute treat?
faqs.a: It treats addiction, mental health concerns and concurrent disorders. Its recovery.com profile lists alcohol, opioids, cocaine, methamphetamine, benzodiazepines and prescription drugs among the substances, and anxiety, depression, PTSD and trauma among the mental health conditions.

Every participant has lifetime access to continuing care after residential treatment. A continuing care coordinator helps you plan for home before discharge, and the centre's recovery.com profile mentions online follow-up sessions, aftercare groups and recovery coaching.

Yes. The Family Freedom Program is a free weekly session on Zoom every Monday at 5:30 p.m. Pacific Time. It covers topics such as acceptance, anger, attachment and codependency, and families can join while their loved one is in treatment or afterwards.
